```c
void foo(int n) {
  int x = 0;
  while (x < n) {
    x = x + 1;
  }
  // post-condition
  if (x != n) {
    //@ assert(n < 0);
  }
}
```

Add a loop annotation block immediately before the `while (x < n)` line (the `while` keyword is on line 11 in the slice file; verify the exact line with `read`). The annotation must make WP prove the final `assert(n < 0)`.

Semantics required: after the loop, we know `x >= n` (negated loop guard). To also prove `x != n ==> n < 0`, the loop invariant must additionally establish that whenever `x <= n` holds together with `x >= n` we get `x == n`, otherwise `n < 0`. A valid set of annotations is:
- `loop invariant x >= 0;`
- `loop invariant x <= n || n < 0;`
- `loop assigns x;`
- `loop variant n - x;`

You may adjust expressions if WP requires, but do NOT add any `admit`, `assume`, or `axiom` — those are forbidden. Do NOT modify the original C tokens or the original assertion. Only add ACSL comments.
